 View Comments Leah B. Foley, United States Attorney District of Massachusetts looked over at John Soars, Assistant Special Agent in Charge of Homeland Security Investigations in New England as he spoke during a press conference at Moakley Federal Courthouse in Boston, on Oct. 20. The United States Attorney’s held the press conference to announce the dismantling of an alleged marriage fraud ring that arranged hundreds of fake marriages in Massachusetts that were designed to obtain unlawful immigration benefits. Jessica Rinaldi/Globe Staff Six women have been charged with arranging “sham marriages” for illegal immigrants throughout Massachusetts for more than a decade, raking in profits of more than $6 million, according to federal officials . 
 The alleged ringleader, Jennifer Gonzalez, 43, of Fall River, is accused of arranging 18 to 20 marriages a year, charging customers between $38,000 and $40,000, and using most of her profits to buy land in the Dominican Republic, according to US Attorney Leah B. Foley. 
 A photo of an alleged fake marriage taking place was seen as Leah B. Foley spoke to reporters. Jessica Rinaldi/Globe Staff “It is alleged that Ms. Gonzalez got rich off selling the American dream, all the while investing her money in another country,” Foley said during a press conference Wednesday announcing the charges. 
 She called the alleged scheme “an affront” and “disheartening to those who follow our country’s laws” when applying for citizenship as the spouse of an American citizen. 
 Most of the men who paid to marry American women were Brazilian nationals seeking green cards that would allow them to stay in the country legally, according to federal officials. 
 This story will be updated when more information is released.
